title: Mughal Monuments in India: A Heritage Trail
seoTitle: Mughal Monuments in India: Tombs, Forts & Gardens | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Mughal monuments in India: Humayun's Tomb, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri, Akbar's tomb, the Baby Taj, the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Jama Masjid and Kashmir's gardens.
description: A guide to Mughal monuments in India, in the order they were built: Humayun's Tomb, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri under Akbar, Akbar's tomb at Sikandra, Itmad-ud-Daulah, the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi, the Mughal gardens of Kashmir and Pinjore, Bibi ka Maqbara and Safdarjung's Tomb, with how to see them on a trip.
dek: The Mughals built some of India's most famous monuments between the 16th and 18th centuries. Seen in order, they tell the story of a style.

hero.alt: Bastions of the red sandstone walls of Agra Fort

intro: The Mughal dynasty, founded by Babur after the battle of Panipat in 1526, ruled much of the subcontinent until the 18th century and nominally until 1857. Its builders brought together Persian, Central Asian and Indian traditions in tombs, forts, mosques and gardens.

Seeing the monuments roughly in the order they were built shows how the style grew, from the red sandstone and marble of Humayun's Tomb to the white marble of the Taj Mahal. Most are concentrated in Delhi, Agra and Fatehpur Sikri.
quickAnswer: The major Mughal monuments are Humayun's Tomb and the Red Fort in Delhi; Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal, Itmad-ud-Daulah and Akbar's tomb at Sikandra in and around Agra; Fatehpur Sikri; the Jama Masjid in Delhi; the Mughal gardens of Srinagar; and Bibi ka Maqbara in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar. Five are UNESCO sites: Humayun's Tomb, the Red Fort, Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri.
takeaways: Humayun's Tomb (completed in the 1570s) set the pattern for the Taj Mahal.
Akbar built in red sandstone at Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri.
Itmad-ud-Daulah, the 'Baby Taj', pioneered fine marble inlay.
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and Delhi's Jama Masjid.
Delhi, Agra and Fatehpur Sikri can be seen together in four or five days.

sections.heading: Beyond Delhi and Agra
list: Srinagar's Mughal gardens (Shalimar, Nishat, Chashme Shahi), terraced along the Dal Lake.
Pinjore Gardens near Chandigarh, a Mughal-period terraced garden.
Bibi ka Maqbara in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, often compared with the Taj Mahal.
Lahore, now in Pakistan, has major Mughal monuments too; they are outside this guide.

sections.heading: What to look for
list: The charbagh: a garden divided into four by water channels.
Pietra dura: coloured stones inlaid into marble, perfected at Itmad-ud-Daulah and the Taj.
Double domes, which let the outside rise high while keeping the inner chamber in proportion.
Calligraphy that seems the same size from top to bottom, because letters higher up are larger.

sections.heading: A short history
paras: Babur's victory at Panipat in 1526 founded the dynasty, but his son Humayun lost the throne to Sher Shah Suri and regained it only in 1555, shortly before his death. Akbar (ruled 1556 to 1605) built the empire's institutions and its first great buildings. Jahangir and Nur Jahan favoured gardens and refined decoration; Shah Jahan (1628 to 1658) built on the grandest scale; and under Aurangzeb building slowed as wars in the Deccan drained resources. After the 18th century the dynasty's power shrank, and the last emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, was exiled by the British after 1857.

safety: Timings, closures and tickets change; check the ASI, state department or temple authority before you go.
The Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays and the Red Fort on Mondays.
Use official ticket sites and licensed guides.
packing: Minimal bags; some monuments restrict large items

faqs.q: What are the most famous Mughal monuments?
faqs.a: The Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri and Delhi's Jama Masjid.

faqs.q: Which Mughal monuments are UNESCO sites?
faqs.a: Humayun's Tomb, the Red Fort, Agra Fort, the Taj Mahal and Fatehpur Sikri.
Itmad-ud-Daulah in Agra, a marble tomb built by Nur Jahan for her father, completed in 1628.

faqs.q: Which came first, Humayun's Tomb or the Taj Mahal?
faqs.a: Humayun's Tomb, by about 60 years; it influenced the Taj.

faqs.q: How many days do I need?
faqs.a: Four or five days covers Delhi, Agra and Fatehpur Sikri.
